hypothesis: If germ-cell chromosome numbers mostly lie between six and sixteen, most species have a haploid number between 6 and 16, with few species below 6 and fewer still above 16.
pass_criterion: At least 70% of species in the Chromosome Counts Database have a haploid number n between 6 and 16, and the share with n > 16 is below 15% and below the share with n < 6.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of species fall in 6–16, or more than 25% of species have n > 16.
interpretation: 'Germ-nuclei' means gametes, so the haploid number n (half the diploid 2n where only 2n is given). 'Few' is read as under 15%. Polyploid taxa are included, since Thompson did not exclude them. The database mainly covers plants, so the test is on plants.

dataset.name: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB)
dataset.why_it_fits: CCDB has downloadable records of gametic (n) and sporophytic (2n) chromosome counts by taxon, from which a per-species n can be derived.
